summary: Diane A. Lichtenstein completed her PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1977. In 2005, she was attested as an adjunct professor of anthropology at both Baldwin Wallace University and the Cleveland Institute of Art.

Diane E. Riggs is a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD from UCLA in 2010 under William M. Bodiford, held visiting assistant professorships at Pepperdine and Kenyon College, and was attested at Western Michigan University in 2017.
Diane L. Howard is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. She was attested in 1982 as a graduate student at McMaster University, where she studied under Graeme MacQueen.
Dickwela Piyananda is a scholar in Buddhist studies who earned a PhD at the Catholic University of America under the doctoral supervision of Siegfried A. Schulz.
Diego Cosmelli is a philosopher who completed his PhD at the École Polytechnique under the supervision of Francisco Varela.
Diego Loukota is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed an MA at Peking University and earned his PhD from the University of California, Los Angeles, in 2019.

Dieter B. Kapp (1941–2021) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Hermann Berger at the University of Heidelberg (Dr. phil. 1971). He worked at Heidelberg before serving as Director of the Institute for Indology and Tamilistics at Cologne (1990–2006).

Dieter George (1935–1985) was an Indologist. He worked at the Prussian State Library from circa 1972 to 1985 and served as an editor continuing the series Verzeichnis der Orientalischen Handschriften in Deutschland, succeeding Wolfgang Voigt.

Dieter Schlingloff is an Indologist and historian. Educated at Göttingen and Berlin, he taught at Göttingen and Kiel before serving as an honorary professor at the University of Munich (1972–1996) and at the University of Leipzig in 2005.

Dieter Schuh is a Tibetologist who earned his PhD (1972) and Habilitation (1976) at the University of Bonn. He was an adjunct professor of Tibetology at Bonn (1978–2007) and founded and managed the International Institute for Tibetan and Buddhist Studies.

Dietmar Rothermund (1933–2020) was a historian of South Asia and Indologist who earned his PhD from the University of Pennsylvania in 1959. He was the Chair of the History of South Asia at the University of Heidelberg from 1968 to 2001.

Dilgo Khyentse (1910–1991) was a master of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Shechen Gyaltsap Pema Namgyal and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, succeeded Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje from 1987 to 1991, and taught numerous prominent students.

Dilip K. Chakrabarti is a scholar of archaeology and Indology who studied at the University of Calcutta. He taught at Calcutta and the University of Delhi before serving at the University of Cambridge from 1990 to 2008 as Professor of South Asian Archaeology.

Dilip Kumar Biswas (1920–2003) was an Indologist and historian. He studied at Presidency University and the University of Calcutta under Prabodh Chandra Bagchi, and he later held posts at the University of Calcutta and Visva-Bharati University.

Dilli Raman Regmi (1914–2001) was an Indologist and historian. He earned an M.Litt from the University of Madras and a D. Litt. from Patna University in 1961, and he taught at Mahatma Gandhi Kashi Vidyapith.

Dina Bangdel (1964–2017) was an art historian and scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She held academic posts at Ohio State University (circa 2001–2007) and Virginia Commonwealth University (circa 2007–2017).

Dines Andersen (1861–1940) was a Danish Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Copenhagen under Vilhelm Thomsen, Karl Verner, and Michael Viggo Fausbøll. He served as a professor at the University of Copenhagen from 1903 to 1927.

Dineschandra Sircar (1907–1985) was an Indologist and historian. He served as the Government Epigraphist for India and was appointed Carmichael Professor and Head of Ancient Indian History and Culture at the University of Calcutta in 1962.

Ding-hwa Evelyn Hsieh is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. She received her PhD from the University of California, Los Angeles, and was appointed professor of philosophy and religion at Truman State University in 1998.

Dipa Ma (1911–1989) was a Buddhist teacher. She studied under Anagarika Munindra around 1964 and Mahasi Sayadaw around 1967, and she taught students including Sharon Salzberg, Joseph Goldstein, and Sylvia Boorstein.
